claim: Expression of histone H3.3K27M mutant proteins in human diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) results in a global reduction of tri-methylation of H3K27 (H3K27me3).
source: Expression of histone H3.3K27M mutant proteins in human diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) results in a global reduction of tri-methylation of H3K27 (H3K27me3)
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known observation and is supported by data throughout the manuscript including Western blots and ChIP-seq analyses.

claim: H3K27me3 peaks remain at hundreds of genomic loci in DIPG cells despite global reduction.
source: paradoxically, H3K27me3 peaks remain at hundreds of genomic loci
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing retained H3K27me3 peaks in DIPG cells.

claim: The PRC2 complex is sequestered at poised enhancers in H3.3K27M mutant cells.
source: the PRC2 complex is sequestered at poised enhancers, but not at active promoters with high levels of H3.3K27M proteins
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing Ezh2 enrichment at poised enhancers in mutant cells.

claim: The PRC2 complex is not sequestered at active promoters with high levels of H3.3K27M proteins.
source: the PRC2 complex is sequestered at poised enhancers, but not at active promoters with high levels of H3.3K27M proteins
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing H3.3K27M enrichment at active promoters where PRC2 is absent.

claim: The levels of H3.3K27M proteins are low at the retained H3K27me3 peaks.
source: the levels of H3.3K27M proteins are low at the retained H3K27me3 peaks and consequently having minimal effects on the PRC2 activity at these loci
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data comparing H3.3K27M levels at different H3K27me3 peaks.

claim: Low levels of H3.3K27M proteins at retained H3K27me3 peaks have minimal effects on PRC2 activity at these loci.
source: the levels of H3.3K27M proteins are low at the retained H3K27me3 peaks and consequently having minimal effects on the PRC2 activity at these loci
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the observation that H3K27me3 is retained at sites with low H3.3K27M.

claim: H3K27me3-mediated silencing at Wilms Tumor 1 promotes proliferation of DIPG cells.
source: H3K27me3-mediated silencing at specific tumor suppressor genes, including Wilms Tumor 1, promotes proliferation of DIPG cells
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments showing that forced expression of WT1 inhibits DIPG cell proliferation.

claim: More than 75% of DIPG cases contain a somatic mutation of the H3F3A gene leading to H3.3K27M.
source: Recent studies have identified, in more than 75% of DIPG cases, a somatic mutation of the H3F3A gene, leading to a lysine 27 to methionine mutation at histone H3 variant H3.3 (H3.3K27M) (Castel et al., 2015; Schwartzentruber et al., 2012; Sturm et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2012, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: HIST1H3B or HIST1H3C is mutated in a small fraction of DIPG tumors, resulting in the same K to M change.
source: In addition, HIST1H3B or HIST1H3C, one of the 13 genes encoding canonical histone H3.1/H3.2, is also mutated, resulting in the same K to M change in a small fraction of DIPG tumors (Castel et al., 2015; Fontebasso et al., 2014; Solomon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The median survival time after DIPG diagnosis is approximately one year.
source: The median survival time after diagnosis is approximately one year with no cure in sight (Dellaretti et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: H3.3 differs from H3.1/H3.2 by only four or five amino acid residues.
source: H3.3 is a histone H3 variant that differs from H3.1/H3.2 by only four or five amino acid residues (Campos and Reinberg, 2009; Maze et al., 2014; Szenker et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: H3.3 is assembled into nucleosomes in a replication-independent manner.
source: Compared to canonical histone H3.1/H3.2 that is assembled into nucleosomes in a replication-coupled process, histone variant H3.3 is assembled into nucleosomes in a replication-independent manner (Ahmad and Henikoff, 2002a; Tagami et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: H3.3 is enriched at gene promoter and gene body of actively transcribed genes compared to lowly expressed genes.
source: Genome-wide analysis of H3.3 distribution reveals that H3.3 is enriched at gene promoter and gene body of actively transcribed genes compared to lowly expressed genes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: H3K27me2/me3 is catalyzed by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).
source: H3K27me2/me3 is catalyzed by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and plays an important role in the repression of developmentally regulated genes during development (Banaszynski et al., 2013; Cao et al., 2002; Margueron and Reinberg, 2011; Simon and Kingston, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: H3K27me3 is enriched at promoters of silenced genes.
source: H3K27me3 is enriched at promoters of silenced genes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Low levels of H3K27me3 are detected at poised enhancers along with H3K4me1 in mouse and human embryonic stem cells.
source: Moreover, low levels of H3K27me3 are also detected at poised enhancers along with H3K4me1 in mouse and human embryonic stem (ES) cells (Creyghton et al., 2010; Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The PRC2 complex consists of four core subunits (Ezh2, Suz12, EED, and RbAP46/48).
source: The PRC2 complex consists of four core subunits (Ezh2, Suz12, EED, and RbAP46/48), and methylates preferentially nucleosomal histone H3K27.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The PRC2 complex methylates preferentially nucleosomal histone H3K27.
source: The PRC2 complex consists of four core subunits (Ezh2, Suz12, EED, and RbAP46/48), and methylates preferentially nucleosomal histone H3K27.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: H3K27me3 levels are dramatically reduced in DIPG cells expressing H3.3K27M mutant proteins.
source: We and others have found that H3K27me3 levels are dramatically reduced in DIPG cells as well as other tested cell types or organisms expressing H3.3K27M mutant proteins, including mice and Drosophila (Bender et al., 2013; Chan et al., 2013a, 2013b; Funato et al., 2014; Herz et al., 2014; Lewis et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple published studies including the authors' own work.

claim: PRC2 complex binds to H3K27M peptides with high affinity in vitro.
source: For instance, it has been shown that, in vitro, PRC2 complex binds to H3K27M peptides with high affinity (Jayaram et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: H3K27M peptides or mononucleosomes inhibit the enzymatic activity of PRC2 complex in vitro.
source: H3K27M peptides or mononucleosomes inhibit the enzymatic activity of PRC2 complex (Jayaram et al., 2016; Jiao and Liu, 2015; Justin et al., 2016; Lewis et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Ezh2 is enriched at H3.3K27M mononucleosomes compared to wild type H3.3 mononucleosomes isolated from cells.
source: Moreover, Ezh2 is enriched at H3.3K27M mononucleosomes compared to wild type H3.3 mononucleosomes isolated from cells (Bender et al., 2013; Chan et al., 2013a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies including the authors' own work.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins co-localize with active histone mark H3K27ac.
source: For instance, using ChIP-seq, it has been shown that H3.3K27M mutant proteins co-localize with active histone mark H3K27ac where the PRC2 complex should be absent (Piunti et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The PRC2 complex binds H3K27M mononucleosomes with equal affinity as wild type nucleosomes.
source: Moreover, the PRC2 complex binds H3K27M mononucleosomes with equal affinity as wild type nucleosomes (Herz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: H3K27me3 is retained or elevated at the promoters of a small coterie of genes in DIPG xenograft cell lines harboring H3.3K27M mutation.
source: In addition to the global loss of H3K27me3, we and others observed that H3K27me3 is retained or elevated at the promoters of a small coterie of genes in DIPG xenograft cell lines harboring H3.3K27M mutation (Bender et al., 2013; Chan et al., 2013a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies including the authors' own work.

claim: Genes with retained H3K27me3 in DIPG cells are enriched in cancer pathways.
source: Moreover, gene etiology analysis indicates that these genes are enriched in cancer pathways.
evidence: This is stated based on gene etiology analysis mentioned in the introduction.

claim: Ezh2 is required for tumorigenesis of DIPG in a mouse model.
source: Supporting this model, it has been shown that Ezh2 is required for tumorigenesis of DIPG in a mouse model (Mohammad et al., 2017; Piunti et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Ezh2 and H3K27me3 silence the tumor suppressor gene p16 in DIPG cells.
source: It has been shown that Ezh2 and H3K27me3 silence the tumor suppressor gene (TSG) p16 (Cordero et al., 2017; Mohammad et al., 2017; Piunti et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins are enriched at highly expressed genes in SF7761 cells.
source: The H3.3K27M mutant proteins were enriched at actively transcribed genes compared to lowly expressed genes in both SF7761 and SF8628 cells (Figure 1A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins are enriched at highly expressed genes in SF8628 cells.
source: The H3.3K27M mutant proteins were enriched at actively transcribed genes compared to lowly expressed genes in both SF7761 and SF8628 cells (Figure 1A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The localization pattern of H3.3K27M mutant proteins is similar to wild type H3.3 proteins.
source: a pattern that is similar to the localization pattern of wild type H3.3 proteins detected in other cell lines (Banaszynski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by comparison to published data.

claim: H3K27M antibodies do not detect signals in human neural stem cells with wild type H3.
source: Under the same conditions, ChIP-seq signals in human neural stem cells (NSCs) with wild type H3 were not detected using the same H3K27M antibodies (Figure 1C), supporting the idea that H3.3K27M ChIP-seq signals detected in SF7761 and SF8628 are specific.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins are enriched at highly transcribed genes in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
source: H3.3K27M mutant proteins in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells were also enriched at promoters and gene bodies of actively transcribed genes compared to lowly expressed genes (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Two independent H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cell clones were generated using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: we introduced the same heterozygous mutation at the H3F3A gene in mouse ES cells using the CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing technology and isolated two independent clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells grew like wild type mouse ES cells.
source: The two H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells grew like wild type mouse ES cells and had normal karyotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells had normal karyotype.
source: The two H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells grew like wild type mouse ES cells and had normal karyotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by karyotype data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: H3K27me1 was not affected to a detectable degree in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
source: Compared to wild type cells, H3K27me1 was not affected to a detectable degree in H3.3K27M mutant cells under all these conditions, consistent with published study in DIPG cells (Bender et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data and citation to published study.

claim: H3K27me2 levels were reduced dramatically in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells compared to wild type cells.
source: In contrast, H3K27me2 and H3K27me3 levels, while detectable in high amounts of cell extracts, were reduced dramatically in H3.3K27M mutant cells compared to wild type cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: H3K27me3 levels were reduced dramatically in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells compared to wild type cells.
source: In contrast, H3K27me2 and H3K27me3 levels, while detectable in high amounts of cell extracts, were reduced dramatically in H3.3K27M mutant cells compared to wild type cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The reduction of H3K27me2/me3 in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells is unlikely due to reduced levels of the PRC2 complex.
source: Moreover, the reduction of H3K27me2/me3 in each of the H3.3K27M mutant ES cell clone is unlikely due to the reduced levels of the PRC2 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: 29,424 H3.3K27M ChIP-seq peaks were identified in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1.
source: H3.3K27M ChIP-seq identified 29,424 and 27,048 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1 and #2, respectively
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 27,048 H3.3K27M ChIP-seq peaks were identified in H3.3K27M mutant clone #2.
source: H3.3K27M ChIP-seq identified 29,424 and 27,048 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1 and #2, respectively
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 22,959 H3.3K27M ChIP-seq peaks overlapped between the two H3.3K27M mutant clones.
source: of which 22,959 peaks overlapped.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: About 4,555 H3.3K27M false-positive peaks were identified in wild type mouse ES cells.
source: About 4,555 H3.3K27M false-positive peaks were identified in wild type mouse ES cells and few of these peaks overlapped with H3.3K27M ChIP-seq peaks identified in H3.3K27M mutant cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: 30,295 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in wild type mouse ES cells.
source: We identified 30,295 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in wild type mouse ES cells, 17,158 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1 and 16,316 in H3.3K27M mutant clone #2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 17,158 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1.
source: We identified 30,295 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in wild type mouse ES cells, 17,158 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1 and 16,316 in H3.3K27M mutant clone #2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 16,316 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in H3.3K27M mutant clone #2.
source: We identified 30,295 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in wild type mouse ES cells, 17,158 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant clone #1 and 16,316 in H3.3K27M mutant clone #2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Almost all H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in H3.3K27M mutant lines overlapped with those identified in wild type mouse ES cells.
source: Almost all H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in each H3.3K27M mutant lines overlapped with those identified in wild type mouse ES cells (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H3K27me3 levels at all peaks in H3.3K27M mutant lines were reduced compared to wild type mouse ES cells.
source: Moreover, compared to wild type mouse ES cells, H3K27me3 levels at all of these peaks in H3.3K27M mutant lines were reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 40% of the overlapped Ezh2 peaks between two H3.3K27M mutant clones were unique in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
source: Surprisingly, we observed a dramatic increase of the Ezh2 ChIP-seq peak numbers in each of the H3.3K27M mutant clones. Specifically, 40% of the overlapped Ezh2 peaks between two H3.3K27M mutant clones were unique in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells, and were not detected in wild type mouse ES cells using the same cut off.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Ezh2 proteins are redistributed to new locations in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
source: This result suggests that Ezh2 proteins, most likely the PRC2 complexes, are redistributed to new locations but do not generate new H3K27me3 peaks in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the ChIP-seq data showing unique Ezh2 peaks in mutant cells.

claim: H3.3K27M reads density was significantly higher at Ezh2 peaks unique in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells than those found in both wild type and mutant ES cells.
source: First, we compared the levels of H3.3K27M and H3K27me3 at these two groups of Ezh2 peaks, and found that the H3.3K27M reads density was significantly higher at Ezh2 peaks unique in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells than those found in both wild type and mutant ES cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: H3K27me3 levels at Ezh2 peaks unique to H3.3K27M mutant cells were dramatically reduced compared to wild type cells.
source: Interestingly, similar analysis on the published dataset using HA- and EYFP-tagged H3.3 proteins in mouse ES cells showed that wild type H3.3 was enriched to a similar level between these two groups of Ezh2 peaks (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C). The difference in the enrichment of H3.3K27M and wild type H3.3 at these two groups of Ezh2 peaks is currently unknown. Nonetheless, compared to wild type cells, H3K27me3 levels at the Ezh2 peaks unique to H3.3K27M mutant cells were dramatically reduced in the H3.3K27M mutant cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Ezh2 peaks unique to H3.3K27M mutant ES cells overlapped with H3K27me3 and H3K4me1 in wild type ES cells.
source: Surprisingly, the Ezh2 peaks unique to H3.3K27M mutant ES cells were overlapped with H3K27me3 and H3K4me1 in wild type ES cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on analysis of ChIP-seq data overlap.

claim: Chromatin regions containing both H3K4me1 and H3K27me3 are classified as poised enhancers.
source: Chromatin regions containing both H3K4me1 and H3K27me3 are classified as poised enhancers (Creyghton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to published study.

claim: Ezh2 was enriched at three poised enhancers in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells compared to wild type ES cells.
source: Ezh2 was indeed enriched at all three poised enhancers in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells compared to wild type ES cells. In contrast, Ezh2 was reduced at the Hoxa1 promoter, which contained high levels of H3K27me3, in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells compared to wild type ES cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Ezh2 was reduced at the Hoxa1 promoter in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells compared to wild type ES cells.
source: In contrast, Ezh2 was reduced at the Hoxa1 promoter, which contained high levels of H3K27me3, in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells compared to wild type ES cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins were enriched at three poised enhancers compared to the Hoxa1 promoter in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells.
source: H3.3K27M mutant proteins were enriched at these three poised enhancers compared to the Hoxa1 promoter, but to a significantly reduced degree compared to the actively transcribed gene, Actin, in H3.3K27M mutant ES cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: 16,656 Ezh2 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in DIPG line SF8628.
source: Therefore, we used 16,656 Ezh2 ChIP-seq peaks identified in DIPG line, SF8628, and performed unsupervised clustering analysis
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Ezh2 peaks in SF8628 were separated into five different clusters.
source: We observed that Ezh2 peaks were separated into five different clusters (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Cluster 1 and 2 Ezh2 peaks in SF8628 overlapped with H3K27me3 and low levels of H3.3K27M mutant proteins.
source: Cluster 1 and 2 Ezh2 peaks overlapped with H3K27me3 and low levels of H3.3K27M mutant proteins in SF8628 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on clustering analysis.

claim: Three clusters of Ezh2 peaks in SF8628 overlapped with H3.3K27M mutant proteins but with very low levels of H3K27me3.
source: Interestingly, the other three clusters of Ezh2 peaks overlapped with H3.3K27M mutant proteins, but with very low levels of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on clustering analysis.

claim: 2,356 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in SF7761.
source: We identified 2,356 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in SF7761, 5080 peaks in SF8628 and 12,033 peaks in DIPG patient tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 5,080 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in SF8628.
source: We identified 2,356 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in SF7761, 5080 peaks in SF8628 and 12,033 peaks in DIPG patient tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 12,033 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks were identified in DIPG patient tissue.
source: We identified 2,356 H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in SF7761, 5080 peaks in SF8628 and 12,033 peaks in DIPG patient tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: About 9% of H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks in SF7761 or SF8628 exhibited an increased level of H3K27me3 compared to reference cells.
source: About 9% of H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks identified in SF7761 or SF8628, and 6% of H3K27me3 peaks in primary DIPG tissue exhibited an increased level of H3K27me3 compared to the reference cells or reference brain tissue, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: About 6% of H3K27me3 peaks in primary DIPG tissue exhibited an increased level of H3K27me3 compared to reference brain tissue.
source: About 9% of H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks identified in SF7761 or SF8628, and 6% of H3K27me3 peaks in primary DIPG tissue exhibited an increased level of H3K27me3 compared to the reference cells or reference brain tissue, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 676 promoters with H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks overlapped among SF7761, SF8628, and primary DIPG tissue.
source: Importantly, of all the promoters with H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks, 676 promoters overlapped among these three samples (Figure 3A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Gene promoters with the least reduced H3K27me3 had lower levels of H3.3K27M mutant proteins than those with most reduced H3K27me3 in H3.3K27M mutant mouse ES cells.
source: The gene promoters with the least reduced H3K27me3 had lower levels of H3.3K27M mutant proteins than those with most reduced H3k27me3 in mutant cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Gene promoters with the least reduced H3K27me3 in H3.3K27M mutant cells had higher levels of H3K27me3 in wild type cells than gene promoters with the most reduced H3K27me3.
source: Moreover, we also compared the H3K27me3 ChIP-seq read density at the promoters of these two groups of genes in wild type ES cells (Figure 3E) and found that gene promoters with the least reduced H3K27me3 in H3.3 K27M mutant cells had higher levels of H3K27me3 in wild type cells than the gene promoters with the most reduced H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins were lower at gene promoters with high levels of H3K27me3 than those with low levels of H3K27me3 in SF8628.
source: We observed that the H3.3K27M mutant proteins were lower at the gene promoters with high levels of H3K27me3 than those with low levels of H3K27me3 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Analysis of H3K27me3 and H3.3K27M datasets in SF7761 supported the same conclusion as SF8628.
source: Analysis of the H3K27me3 and H3.3K27M datasets obtained in SF7761 supported the same conclusion (Figure 3H and I and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3H and I.

claim: 80 of the 676 genes with H3K27me3 peaks in three DIPG samples are tumor suppressor genes.
source: Based on the annotation of three different databases, we found that 80 of the 676 genes are TSGs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The expressions of NGFR, WT1 and MME were lowest among 12 genes in tumor cells.
source: While the expression of these 12 genes in all these tumor lines was low in general, clustering analysis showed that the expressions of NGFR, WT1 and MME were lowest among these 12 genes in these tumor cells, irrespectively mutation status of histone H3, when compared with human NSCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Depletion of Suz12 increases the expression of WT1 in SF7761 and SF8628 cells.
source: Depletion of Suz12 using two independent shRNAs resulted in increased expression of all these four genes in two DIPG lines tested (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The expression of WT1 was significantly lower in DIPG tumor samples than NBS-HGG samples.
source: The expression of WT1 and p16 was significantly lower in DIPG tumor samples than NBS-HGG samples (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The expression of p16 was significantly lower in DIPG tumor samples than NBS-HGG samples.
source: The expression of WT1 and p16 was significantly lower in DIPG tumor samples than NBS-HGG samples (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of each WT1 isoform inhibited the proliferation of two H3.3K27M mutant cells.
source: we overexpressed each of the four different isoforms of WT1 in H3.3K27M mutant cells (SF7761 and SF8628) and H3.3 wild type cells (SF9427), and found that the expression of each WT1 isoform inhibited the proliferation of two H3.3K27M mutant cells, but not H3.3 wild type cells (SF9427) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Expression of WT1 isoforms did not inhibit the proliferation of H3.3 wild type cells (SF9427).
source: and found that the expression of each WT1 isoform inhibited the proliferation of two H3.3K27M mutant cells, but not H3.3 wild type cells (SF9427) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Poised enhancers possess a mechanism for the initial recruitment of the PRC2 complex.
source: We propose that the poised enhancers but not active promoters possess a mechanism for the initial recruitment of the PRC2 complex.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed model in the abstract based on the findings.

claim: H3.3K27M mutant proteins help sequester the PRC2 complex to poised enhancers once recruited.
source: Once recruited, the H3.3K27M mutant proteins will help sequester the PRC2 complex to these sites, which reduces the availability of the PRC2 complex at other sites and thereby leads to a global reduction of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed model in the abstract based on the findings.

claim: Sequestration of PRC2 at poised enhancers reduces the availability of the PRC2 complex at other sites.

evidence: This is stated as a proposed model in the abstract based on the findings.

claim: The PRC2 complex is redistributed to poised enhancers in H3.3K27M mutant cells and contributes to tumorigenesis.
